Honestly… the biggest mistake I see is people jumping straight to “marketing” before their systems are dialed in.

You can run great ads or post consistently, but if your follow-up, booking process, and client journey aren’t tight, you’re just leaking money.

What actually works:
• A clear offer people *want* (not just “Botox available”)  
• Fast, consistent follow-up (within minutes, not hours)  
• A simple booking process with reminders to reduce no-shows  
• A way to turn first-time clients into repeat clients  

Once those are solid, *then* marketing starts working the way you expect.

For marketing specifically on a budget:
• Paid ads with a strong offer will outperform “organic only” almost every time  
• Organic content works best as trust-building, not your main lead source  
• You don’t need a big agency… you need someone who understands conversion, not just posting  

If you fix the systems first and then layer in marketing, you’ll see way better ROI and actually fill your schedule instead of just getting likes 👍

Biggest thing… don’t jump straight to marketing.

If your follow-up, booking process, and client journey aren’t solid, you’ll just waste money on ads.

What actually works:
• Strong, clear offer  
• Fast follow-up  
• Easy booking + reminders  

Then layer in marketing:
• Paid ads > organic for new clients  
• Organic builds trust, not volume  

Fix the systems first, then marketing will actually convert 👍
